## Scope verdict: SFCC-795 `ZimmInlineMessage` (commit 8/18, plan step 3.2)

**Verdict: IN SCOPE** — 7 files, all traceable to the plan or its own testing rules; both explicit tiers touched (Tier 2 `product-item/*`, Tier 2 `theme/components/index.ts`) were pre-declared by the plan as unavoidable, no Tier 1 file touched, nothing named as out-of-scope was touched.

### 1. File manifest / tier conformance

What's at stake: an unplanned file is how a one-reviewer PR quietly becomes a four-reviewer PR. What I found: every file in this diff traces cleanly, and I verified this against the actual plan document (`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/plan.md`, §3 "B3" manifest, §4 step 3.2), not just the summary I was handed.

- `product-item/{index.tsx, product-item.css.ts}` (modify, Tier 2/3) and `theme/components/index.ts` (modify, Tier 2) — named explicitly in the B3 manifest.
- `zimmInlineMessage/{index.tsx, index.stories.tsx, zimmInlineMessage.css.ts}` (create, Tier 3) — named explicitly.
- `product-item/{index.stories.tsx, index.test.tsx}` — **not** named in the B3 table for step 3.2, but this is not a gap: I checked the precedent already set on this exact branch. Commit 5 (`9991c918`, step 2.2) touched the identical pair without a separate manifest line either (`git show --stat 9991c918` shows both files touched under an "index.tsx modify" umbrella). The manifest names the primary source file; sibling story/test files travel with it by established convention (`.claude/rules/components.md`) and precedent already in this branch.
- `zimmInlineMessage/index.test.tsx`, `zimmInlineMessage/zimmInlineMessage.css.test.ts`, `product-item/product-item.css.test.ts` — none named in the manifest, but all three are required, not invented: `.claude/rules/testing.md` explicitly says a component with real branching (`ZimmInlineMessage`'s variant→colour switch is exactly that, not "pure prop interpolation") gets its own test regardless of coverage elsewhere; and the plan's own step-3.2 pass criteria #2/#3 use the words "asserted in the recipe test" / "the organism recipe test asserts" — text that has no referent unless these files exist. I opened all three and confirmed each one proves exactly the criterion it's named for (token-not-hex on both variants, no third variant, and the 12px→16px `hasError` branch on `ZimmCartItem`).
- Zero Tier 1 files touched — checked the diff against the full `frozenFiles.md` list by hand (foundation, config, ssr.js, worker/main.js, root package.json, tsconfig, babel.config, workflows, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/CODEOWNERS/.claude/rules) — none appear.
- Nothing from the explicitly-out-of-scope list (`item-variant/*`, `zimmQuantityStepper/`, `zimmCartDrawer/`, `theme/foundation/`, OOS/unavailable detection logic) appears in `git status`.
- No `.claude/registry/*.md` churn present in this diff at all — nothing to note either way.

Fix needed: none.

### 2. The two should-fix fixes

**Component test** (`zimmInlineMessage/index.test.tsx`): 3 tests — verbatim text render, `aria-live="polite"` present, and error/warning resolve to genuinely different computed colours (not just different variant *keys*). This closes exactly the gap named (own-folder proof of aria-live/data-testid/variant difference). Sufficient.

**Stories + gap measurement**: `WithErrorMessage`/`WithWarningMessage` stories exist with correct `message` args (`overrides/app/components/product-item/index.stories.tsx:192-216`). Combined with `product-item.css.test.ts` (proves the token-level branch: `gap` is `var(--zimm-scale-s)` by default/false, `var(--zimm-scale-m)` when `hasError:true`, mobile step untouched) and `index.test.tsx`'s new `useMultiStyleConfig` spy tests (prove `ProductItem` actually calls the recipe with `{hasError: true}` only when `message.variant === 'error'`), the three layers now triangulate the same fact from token, wiring, and visual angles. I did not re-run the live Playwright/Storybook measurement myself — the diff hasn't changed since that was done, and re-running it would be exactly the "identical check against an unchanged diff" the instructions tell me not to repeat. On the paper trail, the fix is complete.

### 3. `hasError` naming, function-form conversion, and the `secondaryActions` DOM-order landmark

Both are sound engineering calls, not deviations needing rework.

- **`hasError`**: I read `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` directly. `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`/`PROP_COMBINATIONS` (lines 226-252) hardcode exactly 5 boolean keys — `inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled` — and exhaustively walk all 2⁵=32 combinations. Naming the new resolution prop anything else (e.g. `isError`) would mean this guard's `true` branch never fires, silently — which is precisely the bug class the guard's own comment documents already happened once for real (`zimmTextInput.css.ts`'s `floated`, line 240-243). Choosing `hasError` deliberately plugs into that existing exhaustive-walk mechanism. I also cross-checked the docblock's claim against `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts` — it genuinely uses `disabled` under the same reasoning, so the precedent cited is real, not fabricated.
- **Function-form `baseStyle`**: the plan's own step-3.2 text says the gap widening "is a recipe state on `ZimmCartItem`, not a prop on the message" — converting from a plain object to a function is literally what that sentence requires, not an invented refactor.
- **`secondaryActions` as the DOM-order landmark**: I read the actual render tree (`product-item/index.tsx:195-264`, unchanged context around the new line 244). `primaryAction` genuinely renders twice via base's pre-existing `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` pattern — once beside the stepper/price on desktop (line 237), once at the very bottom, outside the whole details stack, on mobile (lines 260-264). That arrangement predates this commit and isn't something 3.2 should refactor (Hard Rule #5, Minimal-changes). `secondaryActions` renders exactly once, unconditionally (line 256), making it the only structurally sound single-instance landmark for a `compareDocumentPosition` test. It's disclosed in both the JSX comment (241-243) and the test file's own docblock — not swept under the rug. No different resolution needed.

### 4. `showInventoryMessage` duplication — correctly deferred

I independently verified this rather than taking the report on trust:
- Read the real, unmodified base hook (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product.js:37,73-127`): `showInventoryMessage`/`inventoryMessage` derive from `product.inventory.stockLevel` and `variant.orderable` — real, live SDK data, not a placeholder.
- Grepped the whole `overrides/app` tree for any import of the `product-item` override: zero results. `ProductItem` has no live caller anywhere today.
- Grepped every plan artefact (`plan.md`, `findings.md`, `session-notes.md`) for any prior mention of this overlap: zero hits. This is a genuinely new finding, not a re-litigation of something already decided.

Given no live caller exists, both messages can never actually collide today, and resolving "which one wins" is itself a detection-logic decision the plan explicitly reserves for SFCC-282/796 ("do not wire detection logic"). Fixing it now would mean guessing at a reconciliation nobody has decided — exactly the kind of assumption Hard Rule #12 says to stop and ask about rather than build. Correctly left as a flagged risk, not a defect.

### 5. Fresh read

Verified the two "correctly not fixed" cosmetic items myself rather than trusting the description: read `zimmWishlistBadge.css.ts` directly — confirmed it genuinely has no `defineStyleConfig`/`variants` (plain `baseStyle` object only), so the doc-citation gap is real but exactly as minor as described. Also verified `cart.md` line 70 (CAI-030) genuinely forbids low-stock messaging at cart level, so the "no low-stock variant" pass criterion and its test are grounded in a real requirement, not an invented one. Found nothing else on my own pass through the diff (no leftover `console.log`/TODO, no raw hex in style declarations — only in provenance comments, which is the documented, acceptable pattern).

---

## What Marcel is missing

The "18 commits" framing is already stale, and not because of this commit. Actual `git log develop..HEAD` shows 10 commits landed for the plan's first 7 slots (3 of them loop-driven fix commits not in the original table: `19d9235b`, `662670f8`, `135b1c20` — all legitimate, expected process, not a problem in themselves). If that ratio holds through B4 — the group the plan itself flags as "highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review" with the only adversarial pass — the eventual single PR will likely land closer to 23-25 commits than 18. Worth recalibrating that number now, before it's baked into the PR body or into anyone's mental model of how much review this is.
